summary: We are testing whether an amortized wall-time guard (chrono::steady_clock checked every 512 branch-and-bound nodes, 700ms threshold) combined with fast I/O can reliably achieve a perfect score of 100/100 on the treasure-packing knapsack problem, addressing Docker timing failures that caused iter-2's solution to score 100 only 70% of the time.
key_points: Problem: The existing B&B solver scores 100 locally but sometimes exceeds Docker's 1s wall-time limit. Iter-2 used clock() (CPU time, not wall time) and achieved 100 in only 7/10 runs. A prior iter-3 attempt using per-node chrono checks doubled runtime (~21ms→40ms) due to syscall overhead.

Experiment (single arm, h-main): Modify solution.cpp with 4 targeted changes — (1) record start_time via chrono::steady_clock at main() entry, (2) check elapsed time only every 512 B&B nodes (amortized overhead <0.1ms total vs ~100% for per-node), (3) bail out of B&B if >700ms elapsed, (4) only run post-B&B local search if B&B timed out and <800ms elapsed. Then measure score via the judge script (20 test cases, ~30-45s).

Confirmation: Score of 100 confirms the amortized wall-time guard eliminates Docker timing failures. Score of 95 suggests 700ms threshold is too generous (try 500ms). Score ≤90 suggests a bug in the guard propagation or a regression in solution quality — would require local debugging against all 20 test cases.
